find_files.description: Find visible files below a directory. Both arguments are required: path is a normalized Git-style repository-relative directory using / on every operating system, including Windows (use an empty string for the root); pattern uses the same path format relative to path, where * matches one path segment and ** matches any number of segments (use ** for every descendant). Returns a bounded result set without pagination; when truncated is true, narrow path or pattern and retry.

grep.description: Search visible UTF-8 text without pagination. pattern, path, and file_pattern are required: pattern is a Python regular expression with length limits; path is a repository-relative file or directory and uses an empty string for the repository root; file_pattern is a path-segment-aware glob relative to path and use ** to include every visible file. Scans a bounded amount of text and returns a bounded number of matches; when truncated is true, narrow pattern, path, or file_pattern and retry.

read_file.description: Read a visible file with required path and version current|base|head. The inclusive one-based start_line and end_line may both be omitted for a bounded whole-file read; otherwise both must be provided. Reads a bounded number of lines: current is the verified frozen content and may include the captured overlay; base and head are the pinned Git revisions. Binary files and oversized Snapshot sources are rejected, and output is size-limited; when truncated is true, retry with a narrower explicit line range.

get_diff.description: Read the verified base-to-current diff for one changed visible path. current is frozen Review content and may include the captured workspace overlay, while base is the pinned base revision. Output is size-limited.

comment.description: Submit concrete findings as a bounded batch. Use side=old for removed lines (after - markers) and side=new for added lines (after + markers). existing_code must quote the smallest exact consecutive changed lines on that side, without diff markers or unchanged context. Candidates are resolved independently; rejected_comments reports zero-based input indices and reasons. Retry only rejected indices—accepted items are retained.

review_file_done.description: Declare one or more Review files investigated. reviewed_files must contain a bounded batch of exact paths from review_files. A path is recorded only after a successful model-visible get_diff or read_file call for that path; otherwise the result rejects it in missing_evidence_files. Repeated paths are idempotent.

task_done.description: Attempt to finish the whole investigation. summary is required and length-bounded. The result rejects completion while Review files remain: missing_evidence_files were not successfully viewed with get_diff or read_file; undeclared_files were viewed but not recorded with review_file_done. Continue reviewing and retry task_done. After the configured rejection limit, completion is accepted with incomplete_files so existing findings can still be finalized.

submit_review_plan.description: Add a batch of Reviewer references to the Plan. May be called multiple times to accumulate selections. Duplicates are ignored. Provide a list of reviewer references (e.g. ["security:v1", "performance:v1"]). Each reference must be eligible and not unavailable.

finalize_plan.description: Validate accumulated Reviewers and finalize the Plan. Call this after all submit_review_plan calls are complete. The system validates that the accumulated set exactly matches the eligible reviewers.

verdict.description: Accept or deny one or more finding clusters. Required parameters: cluster_ids (list of cluster identifiers) and action ("accept" or "deny"). Accept publishes the cluster using its canonical candidate fields. Deny suppresses the cluster as a false positive. May be called multiple times to accumulate decisions across different clusters.

merge.description: Merge one or more clusters into a single synthesized Finding. Use when the model should combine candidate attributes across merged clusters rather than accepting canonical fields as-is.

finalize_verdicts.description: Validate that every cluster has received exactly one verdict (accept, deny, or merge) and finalize the verdict set. Call this after all verdict and merge calls are complete. The system validates that all clusters are covered exactly once with no duplicates.
